AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To advocate for the use of a common classification system for Caesarean section across Canada.

AbstractText.Label: OPTIONS
AbstractText.content: A variety of clinical parameters for classification were considered.

AbstractText.Label: OUTCOMES
AbstractText.content: Consideration of a common system for classifying Caesarean section.

AbstractText.Label: EVIDENCE
AbstractText.content: Studies published in English from 1976 to December 2011 were retrieved through searches of Medline and PubMed, using appropriate controlled vocabulary and key words (Caesarean section, vaginal birth after Caesarean, classification) . Results were restricted to systematic reviews, randomized control trials/controlled clinical trials, and observational studies. Grey (unpublished) literature was identified through searching the web sites of health technology assessment and health technology assessment-related agencies, clinical practice guideline collections, clinical trial registries, and the web sites of national and international medical specialty societies .

AbstractText.Label: VALUES
AbstractText.content: The studies reviewed were classified according to criteria described by the Canadian Task Force on Preventive Health Care, and the recommendation for practice ranked according to this classification (Table 1).

AbstractText.Label: SPONSORS
AbstractText.content: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada.

AbstractText.Label: RECOMMENDATION
AbstractText.content: Modified Robson criteria should be used to enable comparison of Caesarean section rates and indications (III-B).

Article.ArticleTitle: No. 281-Classification of Caesarean Sections in Canada: The Modified Robson Criteria.

Journal.Title: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
